ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: As shown in the diagram, four triangular paper pieces $\triangle ABC$, $\triangle AB_{1}C_{1}$, $\triangle AB_{2}C_{2}$, and $\triangle AB_{3}C_{3}$ are perfectly superimposed and arranged as depicted. Given $BC=\sqrt{10}$ and $AB=1$, what is the area of quadrilateral $CC_{1}C_{2}C_{3}$?
ready1_open_rewrite.raw_answer_text:
\textbf{Solution:} From the given problem, we have Rt$\triangle ABC \cong$ Rt$\triangle AB_{1}C_{1} \cong$ Rt$\triangle AB_{2}C_{2} \cong$ Rt$\triangle AB_{3}C_{3}$,\\
$\therefore AC = AC_{1} = AC_{2} = AC_{3}$, and AB$ = AB_{1} = 1$.\\
In Rt$\triangle ABC$, by the Pythagorean theorem, we have $AC = \sqrt{BC^{2} - AB^{2}} = 3$,\\
$\therefore Area_{\text{quadrilateral} CC_{1}C_{2}C_{3}} = 4 \times \frac{3 \times 3}{2} = \boxed{18}$.

ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: In the figure, four triangles are arranged around the common point A. C is directly above A, C2 is directly below A, C1 is on the left side of A, and C3 is on the right side of A; therefore quadrilateral CC1C2C3 is a rhombus/kite-shaped outer frame, whose two diagonals CC2 and C1C3 are vertical and horizontal respectively, and intersect perpendicularly at A. Point B is on the right side of A, AB is a horizontal line segment; point C is above A, AC is a vertical line segment, so △ABC is a right triangle, with the right angle at A. Reasoning: The four triangular paper pieces completely coincide and are then arranged, so △ABC, △AB1C1, △AB2C2, △AB3C3 are congruent, and all are right triangles. Given BC = √10, AB = 1. In Rt△ABC, by the Pythagorean theorem, AC = √(BC^2 - AB^2) = √(10 - 1) = 3. By congruence, AC = AC1 = AC2 = AC3 = 3. Therefore the vertical diagonal CC2 of quadrilateral CC1C2C3 = AC + AC2 = 3 + 3 = 6, and the horizontal diagonal C1C3 = AC1 + AC3 = 3 + 3 = 6. The two diagonals are perpendicular, so the area = 1/2 × 6 × 6 = 18.
